overall_summary: Bitcoin is soft under 80k as the Fed meeting gets underway, but spot ETF inflows and Ripple’s regulatory win keep institutional tone constructive. Macro is mixed—solid regional Fed data versus sticky inflation, high yields, and a firm dollar. Geopolitics stay noisy with elections and strikes, offset only partly by Iran de-escalation talks.
key_points: BTC ETFs take $110M; Ripple wins OCC nod
Fed FOMC starts; pause odds high but hawkish risks
Galaxy calls BTC bear market over since June
Mixed whale moves; geo tensions vs diplomacy hopes

items.title: Bitcoin slips under $80,000 as Fed meeting begins
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped about 0.4 percent since midnight UTC to near 79,700 dollars on Tuesday, lagging a rally in Asian tech stocks. The Federal Reserve starts its two-day policy meeting today with the rate decision due Wednesday; markets price roughly a 90 percent chance of no change but will parse any December hike signals. Liquidations eased while futures volume rose, and traders are watching whether the 79,000 to 80,000 zone holds into the announcement. This is the key macro catalyst that can drive the next directional move for crypto risk assets.
items.impact: Elevated volatility into Wednesday Fed decision; support test unresolved

items.title: US spot Bitcoin ETFs take in $110 million Monday
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded 110 million dollars in net inflows on October 26, ending a two-day outflow streak, with the entire amount going into BlackRock's IBIT. October remains net negative at roughly 202 million dollars of outflows month-to-date after heavy withdrawals earlier. Fresh creations force actual Bitcoin buying and signal that institutional demand reappeared on the dip. Traders watch whether the inflow streak continues after the Fed decision as a gauge of sustained demand.
items.impact: Supports price via forced spot buying if inflows persist

items.title: Ripple wins final OCC approval for national trust bank
items.summary: The OCC granted Ripple final approval to open Ripple National Trust Bank, completing the process after conditional approval last December. The federally supervised bank will manage RLUSD stablecoin reserves, act as collateral trustee, and offer fiduciary digital-asset custody while issuance stays with the New York-regulated entity. This is a clear regulatory win that brings a major stablecoin and custody operation under federal oversight and could ease institutional adoption. XRP and related names often react positively to such clarity, and it sets a template for other crypto firms seeking bank charters.
items.impact: Positive for RLUSD, XRP, and broader crypto banking legitimacy

items.title: Galaxy Research says Bitcoin bear market ended in June
items.summary: Galaxy Research head Alex Thorn argued the Bitcoin bear market bottomed in June and the asset has entered an accumulation phase, calling current levels an attractive time to buy and hold. The firm cited five straight weekly closes above the 50-week moving average after 44 weeks below it, fading long-term holder selling, and a stronger debasement case from rising US debt. A weekly close below roughly 76,540 that is not quickly regained would challenge the view. This is a high-profile institutional research call that can influence positioning among funds and larger traders.
items.impact: Supports dip-buying narrative and longer-term accumulation bias

items.title: Dormant whale withdraws 11,330 BTC from Binance
items.summary: A Bitcoin whale inactive for five months withdrew 11,330 BTC worth roughly 900 million dollars from Binance, according to on-chain monitors. Large exchange withdrawals reduce available sell-side supply and are often read as self-custody or accumulation rather than immediate distribution. The size stands out amid quiet price action near 80,000 and adds to other recent large holder movements. Traders should care because sustained whale outflows can tighten float and amplify any upside move once macro risk clears.
items.impact: Removes supply from exchange; potential accumulation signal

items.title: Two dormant whales send 2,571 BTC to Coinbase Prime
items.summary: Two Bitcoin wallets dormant since 2023 moved a combined 2,571 BTC worth about 206 million dollars into Coinbase Prime within minutes of each other. Coinbase Prime serves institutional custody and OTC flow, so the coins could be headed for a block sale, rebalancing, or simple custody change rather than open-market dumping. Still, large transfers to exchange-linked platforms raise short-term supply-risk flags when Bitcoin is already testing support. Watch Coinbase premium and spot order flow for confirmation of any selling.
items.impact: Potential near-term supply overhang if coins are sold OTC or on-exchange

items.title: Fed FOMC meeting starts; 90% odds of rate pause
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's two-day October meeting begins today with the rate decision due Wednesday. Markets price roughly a 90 percent chance of holding the funds rate in the 3.75 to 4.00 percent range after September's hike. Traders will scrutinize Chair Kevin Warsh's statement and press conference for any hawkish tilt toward a possible December move, especially with sticky inflation and midterm elections days away. Crypto and risk assets are watching for guidance that could shift rate-cut or hike bets and move the dollar and yields.
items.impact: High event risk for yields, DXY and Bitcoin direction into Wednesday

items.title: US 10-year yield near 5%, DXY holds above 102
items.summary: The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield is little changed around 4.98 to 5.00 percent while the dollar index sits firm near 102, close to recent highs. Support comes from still-elevated inflation concerns and positioning ahead of the Fed decision. Higher yields and a strong dollar typically tighten financial conditions and weigh on risk assets. Crypto traders should note that any hawkish Fed surprise could push yields and the greenback higher still.
items.impact: Firm yields and dollar act as headwind for Bitcoin and equities

items.title: Dallas Fed manufacturing activity beats forecasts
items.summary: The Dallas Fed's Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey general business activity index rose to 13.4 in October from 9.8, beating the 7.0 consensus. Production slowed but stayed solidly positive while future activity expectations improved sharply. Input price pressures remain elevated, however. The stronger regional print supports the soft-landing growth narrative and could keep the Fed data-dependent rather than urgently hawkish.
items.impact: Positive growth signal may support risk appetite if confirmed by national data

items.title: Chicago Fed activity index turns positive
items.summary: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index rose to plus 0.07 in September from a revised minus 0.08, beating the minus 0.1 expectation and signaling slightly above-trend growth. Production drove the gain while consumption and housing dragged. The three-month average edged up to plus 0.03. This modest improvement aligns with resilient Q3 growth expectations and reduces immediate recession fears ahead of Thursday's GDP print.
items.impact: Supports soft-landing view, mildly positive for risk assets

items.title: Key US data due today: durables, confidence, home sales
items.summary: Markets are focused on Tuesday's slate of Durable Goods Orders for September, Conference Board Consumer Confidence for October, and New Home Sales for September, plus Case-Shiller home prices. These releases land while the FOMC is meeting and will help shape views on business investment, consumer health and housing before the Fed decision and Thursday's GDP and PCE. Traders should watch for surprises that alter December rate-hike odds or growth forecasts.
items.impact: Data surprises could swing yields and risk sentiment intraday

items.title: Sticky inflation and oil keep Fed on hawkish watch
items.summary: Despite the expected October pause, analysts and markets still see a December hike as live because September inflation accelerated and oil prices remain elevated on Middle East tensions. Consumer sentiment is near multi-year lows on affordability worries. Chair Warsh will face pressure to explain any hold without damaging the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility just before midterms. This backdrop keeps longer-term rate expectations elevated and limits how far risk assets can run on a simple pause.
items.impact: Limits dovish relief; sustains higher-for-longer pressure on crypto

items.title: Israel Votes in High-Stakes Election Testing Netanyahu
items.summary: Israelis are heading to the polls today in the first national election since the October 7 2023 attacks, with record early turnout. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces a tight race against former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, and neither bloc looks set for a clear majority. The outcome will shape Israel's approach to Gaza, Iran, and regional security just as US midterms approach. Traders should watch because a Netanyahu win could mean more hawkish moves on Iran while a change could ease some tensions but still leave coalition uncertainty that keeps risk premiums elevated.
items.impact: Elevated Middle East risk premium and oil volatility until coalition clarity

items.title: Mecca Pact Powers Meet Iran in Tehran De-Escalation Push
items.summary: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey held talks in Tehran with Iranian leaders on Monday aimed at preventing a return to full-scale US-Israeli-Iran fighting. The sides agreed to keep dialogue going on regional security as Houthi attacks on Saudi targets continue and oil flows through Hormuz stay disrupted. Markets took some comfort, with Brent crude easing from recent multi-month highs near 117 dollars. Crypto traders care because successful de-escalation would lower energy inflation fears and support risk assets, while failure keeps the black-swan oil shock alive.
items.impact: Oil price pullback reduces inflation drag and supports risk-on sentiment

items.title: Oil Eases as Diplomacy Hopes Offset Hormuz and Houthi Risks
items.summary: Brent crude slipped from six-month highs toward the mid-110s as Tehran talks and mediation efforts raised hopes of avoiding wider escalation, even as Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure and airports persist. Hormuz shipping remains well below normal and inventories are tight, so the market is still vulnerable. For Bitcoin and risk assets this matters because sustained high oil feeds inflation and tighter financial conditions, while any clear de-escalation would be a relief rally catalyst.
items.impact: Range-bound oil keeps macro uncertainty high for risk assets

items.title: Lula Wins Historic Fourth Term as Bolsonaro Rejects Result
items.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva secured a dramatic runoff victory over Flavio Bolsonaro with about 51.8 percent of the vote, becoming the first to win after losing a first round in modern Brazilian history. Bolsonaro refused to concede and moved to challenge the result after extended voting hours, while markets had priced in a right-wing win. The Brazilian real and local assets took a hit. Crypto traders should note the political uncertainty in a major emerging market and commodity exporter, plus any Trump reaction that could spill into broader trade or Latin America risk sentiment.
items.impact: EM currency and equity volatility; potential regional political risk premium

items.title: UN Inquiry Accuses Israel of Ongoing Gaza Genocide
items.summary: A UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry reported on Monday that Israel continued genocidal acts in Gaza even after a prior ceasefire and also committed crimes against humanity including extermination in the West Bank. Israel dismissed the findings as a misinformation campaign. The report lands on the day of Israel's election and adds to international legal and diplomatic pressure. For markets it raises the chance of further sanctions, isolation, or secondary boycotts that could hit Israeli-linked assets and keep Middle East risk elevated.
items.impact: Heightened sanctions and isolation risk around Israel and related assets

items.title: Jordan Launches Airstrikes in Syria After Church Attack
items.summary: Jordan carried out airstrikes on what it called terrorist hideouts in southern Syria in retaliation for a deadly shooting at a Christian church funeral that killed nine people. Syrian authorities reported civilian deaths including children and closed border crossings, while Jordan said it had coordinated but Damascus disputed that. The episode adds another flashpoint on an already tense regional map. Traders should monitor it as a sign of spreading instability that could complicate oil transit and broader Middle East risk pricing.
items.impact: Additional regional military friction raises black-swan tail risks
